px_A_external: Measured data (E-MEXP-668, external). (a) Paired difference in within-guide Spearman correlation between predicted affinity score and measured repression, corrected minus uncorrected, for each of the 12 external guide families; the uncorrected baseline for each family is in brackets on the axis. The three site-class offsets were fitted on GSE5814 alone and frozen. Differences are plotted rather than the two absolute curves because the two models differ by about 1e-4 against correlations of about 3e-2 and would otherwise be indistinguishable. 11 of 12 families move the wrong way. (b) The paired family-cluster bootstrap, 5000 resamples, of the equal-family mean difference. The observed effect is -1.06e-04 with interval -1.67e-04 to -3.28e-05. The correction does not improve external ranking; the interval excludes zero on the side of no benefit and the magnitude is negligible against a baseline correlation of 0.028.
px_B_approx: Model calculation on measured inputs. Audit of the compressed equilibrium solve, drawn only from audited outputs. (a) Development selection surface: 90th-percentile focal occupancy error against the full retrieved reference over the 8 development families, for every configuration on the frozen grid; the circled point is the selected configuration (bins, $R=100$, $B=100$), chosen before any held-out family was scored and not reselected afterwards. (b) On the 54 held-out cases from 7 independent families, the two residual definitions, each divided by $\max(M,1)$, are separated by 11.7 orders of magnitude at the median: the compressed system is solved to 2.7e-16 at worst, but the resulting solution misses the original conservation law by a median of 1.7e-05 and by up to 2.0e-03. The second quantity is the approximation error; the first only says the bisection converged. (c) Median forward cost in milliseconds at matched outputs on one construct with 4919 competitors, single-threaded float64; bin construction is part of preparation, not an addition to it. Compression does not pay for itself at this workload: the selected configuration's cached solve is 0.28 ms slower than the full solve, so preparation never pays back; truncation is cheaper from the first solve but fails the gradient target. (d) Analytic gradients against central differences over 17 coordinates, including omitted ones; worst relative error 0.0433 overall and 0.00144 over the 13 coordinates whose gradient exceeds 1e-9. The dotted line is equality.
fig_approx: Model calculation on measured inputs. Compressing the competitor set, on 54 held-out cases from 7 guide families disjoint from the 8 used to choose the configuration. (a) Relative error against the full retrieved reference at depth $R=100$, one point per case; dotted lines are the 1% engineering targets, so only the lower-left quadrant passes both. (b) Two error measures for the same solutions, each divided by $\max(M,1)$; boxes are median and quartiles. (c) Median forward time in milliseconds over 50 repetitions on one construct with 4919 competitors, single-threaded float64; bin construction is part of preparation.
